Entrepreneurship & Marketing 9.desc: This course surveys two main areas: entrepreneurship and marketing. Students will learn about opportunities for entrepreneurship and characteristics of entrepreneurs while developing their own entrepreneurial skills. Innovation and invention along with ways to add value to existing products will be a focus. Students will also learn about the strategies and planning involved in successfully marketing a product. Most coursework is project-based with students being presented with opportunities to think critically, ethically, and flexibly about business activities; collaborate effectively and empathically; manage their time; and be creative in areas that interest them in the field of business. This course is an excellent foundation for senior business courses such as Marketing 11 & Economics 12.

Computer Studies 9.desc: This course surveys two main areas: information & communication technologies, and media art. Information and Communication Technologies 9 involves the development of much need desktop publishing skills as well as further work in developing the ability to create multi-media projects for various purposes including: advertising, presenting, and organizing information. The course gives the students an opportunity to explore both the software and hardware aspects of all computers, and how we can connect them. As well, students will be exposed to a number of applications that help them learn to program and design web sites. Most work in the course is project-based and requires students to think critically, problem solve, be flexible and be creative. Effective time management & ethical issues related to technology will be addressed in this course. Once students take Grade 9 IT then CIS 11 is the next option.

Data Science, Python & AI 11.desc: This ADST 11 course will introduce students to the main ideas in data science through free tools such as Google Sheets, Python, Data Commons and Tableau. Students will learn to be data explorers in project-based units, through which they will develop their understanding of data analysis, sampling, correlation/causation, bias and uncertainty, probability, modeling with data, making and evaluating data-based arguments, the power of data in society, and more. Students will also use AI generative tools to further develop their abilities to write prompts and use these tools in academically appropriate ways.

Woodwork 9.desc:
$100 Course Fee Applies. This course is designed to build upon skills learned from ADST 9 Woodwork. Students will identify sources of inspiration and work towards developing designs which consider how tools and materials can be effectively repurposed and recycled. As students learn and build their understanding, they will learn a series of skills and techniques which will allow them to create increasingly complex products or prototypes. Once the course has been completed, the students are expected to know the following:
• identification, characteristics, properties, and uses of wood from various species
• choices related to the sustainable use of wood uses and creation of plans and drawings
• techniques for stock breakout and woodworking
• using a variety of tools and equipment, including stationary power equipment
• choices for planning, drawing, and constructing a project
• functions and role of portable and stationary power equipment in the creation of a project
• functions of hand tools

Youth Work in Trades.desc: Youth Work in Trades allows students to earn dual credit—high school credit and credit toward an apprenticeship through SkilledTradesBC. Students secure a paid position in a recognized trade, register as apprentices, and begin accumulating the work-based training hours required for nationally recognized trade credentials. Students earn 4 high school credits for every 120 hours of paid work, up to 16 credits while in secondary school. Work schedules are flexible: students may work after school, evenings, weekends, holidays, or even during part of the school day. Examples of eligible trades include Arborist, Automotive Service Technician, Cook, Construction, Electrical, Horticulture, Forestry, and Hair Stylist.

Français langue 10.desc: The Grade 10 program is a combined literature/language course. In the literature component, students continue their study of novels, poetry, drama, and expository and informative writing. In addition, they are introduced to both French and French-Canadian literature. Grammatical concepts presented in previous grades are reinforced and students are gradually introduced to more complex syntax analysis. Written compositions (mostly expository) are assigned regularly. Oral presentations continue to form an integral part of course work as does the continued strengthening of speaking and listening skills.

Français langue seconde-immersion 12.desc:
The Grade 12 language arts program will continue to put an equal emphasis on the four language areas: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Language mechanisms presented in previous years are strengthened to develop essay writing skills. Students continue to discover francophone authors, including First Nations writers from the Innu Nation. Students explore how bilingualism plays in their life in order to facilitate decision-making in their personal and working life. Upon completion of Français langue seconde immersion 12 students will also receive credits for French 12.

Students will be offered the opportunity to write the DELF B2 exam for French language certification from the French Ministry of Education.

Physical Education 10: Strength & Power.desc:
$100 Course Fee Applies. This course offers students a unique opportunity to develop sport-specific strength, endurance, power, agility, and overall conditioning within a supportive and structured PE environment. Designed for student-athletes as well as those passionate about strength training, physical wellness, and fitness, this comprehensive branch of PE 10 emphasizes personal physical development in a safe and positive setting.
• Students will focus on improving muscular strength and endurance while deepening their understanding of muscular anatomy and physiology.
• The course also covers key topics such as nutrition, weight training programs, equipment usage, and proper training techniques with an emphasis on safety.
• Students will learn the key components of a well-rounded training program and how to tailor it to meet their personal fitness or athletic goals.
• Guest instructors, including certified personal trainers and fitness coaches, will be invited to share their expertise and provide guidance to help students achieve their fitness goals.

R&B Band 11.desc: Satisfies the Arts Education requirement for graduation. This demanding course will challenge a student's ability to learn by ear, improvise, and perform in a rhythm and blues style. The course offers a chance for students to excel on their instrument or voice and provides opportunities for solos and artistic creativity. In this setting the teacher assumes the role of facilitator, therefore leadership and teamwork skills by the students are a must. Throughout the year, this band will perform at various school and community events as a part of the course, requiring a commitment of availability from all students. This course is open to singers as well as instrumentalists. Enrollment in the course is strictly by consultation with the music teacher, or by in-person or pre-recorded audition.

Composition & Production 12.desc:
Satisfies the Arts Education requirement for graduation Do you make music on your computer, or want to learn how? This non-performance course is perfect for students who are interested in and passionate about music composition and sound production. There is a wide variety of musical genres that may be covered in the course, depending on students’ interest, skills, and previous experience. The course will revolve around three main components: working with and manipulating musical ideas in a digital environment, designing, and altering digital and analogue sound sources, and mixing and mastering live productions and multi-track recordings.

RnB Band Connection: since this course runs in parallel with R&B Band 11/12, there is a limit of 6 students accepted each academic year. Preference will be given to senior grade students who are enrolled in existing Fine Arts (Music or Drama) courses. For performances with the RnB Band, students are to participate in performances and demonstrate light and sound engineering skills, such as operating a mixing board or choreographing stage lighting. All the required skills and techniques will be taught in class.

Please note: This is a bring-your-own-device course, where students will be required to bring a laptop or tablet to class with GarageBand music production software installed (or equivalent, such as FL Studios, Logic Pro, Ableton, BandLab). This course is offered for students in Grades 10-12.

Media Arts 12: Yearbook.desc: Be part of building Sentinel's Yearbook! This is a student-led course made up of five departments: Photography, Photo-editing, Writing, Design, and Business & Marketing. Students choose their department and work together in teams to capture, create, and sell the yearbook. Students learn the technical skills of their department from each other. While there are no pre-requisites, courses in photography, business and leadership are assets. If you are in Grade 8 and are interested, please speak with the yearbook teacher.
